{% extends "docs.html" %} {% from "macros/page.html" import code, page_body, section, toc with context %} {% from "macros/api.html" import options_table %} {% set page_name = "Auto Init" %} {% set page_blurb = "Initialize every registered component with one function call." %} {% block page %} {% call page_body() %} {% call section("introduction", "Introduction", heading=false) %}

Auto Init starts all of the registered Expressive components with a single call. The IIFE bundle exposes it as Expressive.AutoInit.

Importing the JavaScript installs a few document-level behaviors (Forms, Waves, Range, Chips, and Cards), but it does not call AutoInit() for you. Call it after the DOM is ready. This documentation site does that in docs.js on DOMContentLoaded.

{% endcall %} {% call section("initialization", "Initialization") %} {% call code() %} document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() { Expressive.AutoInit(); }); {% endcall %}

Or pass a root element and per-component options. The option keys are the component names from the table below.

{% call code() %} Expressive.AutoInit(document.body, { Menu: { // pass options for Menu here }, FloatingActionButton: { // pass options for FloatingActionButton here } }); {% endcall %}

From the module build:

{% call code() %} import { AutoInit, Tooltip } from './js/expressive.mjs'; AutoInit(); const element = document.querySelector('.custom-tooltip'); Tooltip.init(element, { position: 'top' }); {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("options", "Options") %}

AutoInit(context, options) takes two arguments:

{% call options_table() %} context Element document.body DOM element to search within for components. options Object {} Options for each component, keyed by name. See that component’s page for its own options. {% endcall %}

Calling AutoInit() again on the same elements is safe: each component’s constructor destroys any existing instance on that element before creating a new one.

{% endcall %} {% call section("components", "Components") %}

These are the components AutoInit() starts, and the selector each one claims. Elements that also have no-autoinit are skipped.

Name Selector
Autocomplete.autocomplete
Cards.cards
Carousel.carousel
Chips.chips
Datepicker.datepicker
Menu.menu-trigger
Lightbox.lightboxed
NavigationRail.navigation-rail
Parallax.parallax
ScrollSpy.scrollspy
FormSelectselect
Sidenav.sidenav
Tabs.tabs
Timepicker.timepicker
Tooltip.tooltipped
FloatingActionButton.fixed-action-btn

Snackbar, CharacterCounter, and Range stay out of this table. Range still starts itself when the bundle loads. Forms, Waves, Chips, and Cards also run an import-time Init(); Chips and Cards appear in the table as well so a later AutoInit() can pick up elements added after load.

{% endcall %} {% call section("ignoring", "Ignoring Elements") %}

If you want AutoInit() to skip an element, add the class no-autoinit. Initialize that element yourself with the component’s init method when you need options other than the defaults.

{% call code() %} Hover Expressive.Tooltip.init( document.querySelector('.tooltipped.no-autoinit'), { position: 'top' } ); {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% endblock %}
